exclude: Unchanged across the MAIN depack, outside its upper output boundary and outside the selected sprite block.
Unchanged across MAIN depack. The game replaces the vector locations as part of interrupt setup.
Old BASIC screen and final depacker pull-through stub before the game switches to VIC bank $4000.
extra: Tile glyph layouts and cell colours.

comments.text: Character layouts for tile IDs $00-$3F. Four rows of four glyphs per tile, expanded by $9815.
Four-by-four glyph definitions for tile IDs $40-$7F, the second quarter of the indexed tile table.
Four-by-four glyph definitions for tile IDs $80-$BF, the third quarter of the indexed tile table.
Four-by-four glyph definitions for tile IDs $C0-$FF, the final quarter of the indexed tile table.
Map each glyph byte to the colour RAM value used for the terrain, including replacement cells that enter through scrolling.
Tile indices for map strips $00-$1F. Each strip has 32 entries expanded by $9815.
Tile indices for map strips $20-$3F at the same 32-byte stride.
Tile indices for map strips $40-$47, the end of the six twelve-strip groups.
128 colour entries for glyphs $80-$FF. $9D27 exchanges this block with the upper half of the live terrain colour table at $1880.
Authored character values for the lower part of the visible screen. The title routine reuses its border cells, and the clock and score routines write into the panel during the expedition.
First 128 playfield character glyphs at the $4800 charset base. Each is eight bytes and the field uses VIC multicolour mode.
Upper 128 entries of the scenery glyph address space. Read by character codes $80-$FF when the playfield selects $4800.
Eight bytes of glyph $B5 updated by $9D52 from the selected frame at $85AA.
Seven upper scenery glyph slots between the animated glyph $B5 and the final glyph block.
Scenery glyphs from code $BD through $FF.
Lower 128 tiles of the alternate eight-byte scenery charset. The mode switch at $9D0C selects this charset with $D018 character bits $04.
Upper 128 glyphs of the alternate charset. $9D89 updates the two animated glyphs at $5460.
Sixteen bytes of alternate glyphs $8C and $8D. The updater at $9D89 copies a selected phase from $856A.
Two adjacent bytes inside alternate glyph $FD, set to a pseudo-random byte and its complement by $9D5A.
Sprite slots $60 and $61 at $5800-$587F. The explorer frame generator interleaves a frame into the spare slot and swaps the two sprite selectors.
Sprite slots $62-$6F contain multicolour figures and small creatures. Each slot has 21 rows of three bytes and one pad byte.
Slots $70-$7F show figures, upright scenery, small animals and directional poses.
Slots $80-$8F include tool and creature graphics. In the VIC bank their address is $4000 + 64 times the pointer.
Slots $90-$9F include a key and several large round or stacked objects. The inventory routine uses pointers computed from item IDs.
Slots $A0-$AF hold object shapes such as two diagonal tools, a table-like shape and lettered signs.
Slots $B0-$BF contain object silhouettes and figures. The upper slots are also available to actors.
Slots $C0-$CF contain figures, falling or bent poses, and directional effect shapes.
Slots $D0-$DF include overlay patterns as well as blank and scratch slots. $A3BA clears the visible bytes of slot $D4.
VIC sprite slots $D5-$DF, including blank reserve slots and graphics in the final slots used by the HUD and screen effects.
Lower 128 eight-byte glyphs from the HUD charset. The title printer indexes these by character bytes minus $20.
Upper glyph range of the HUD character address space before the $7FF8 entry stub.
Write $04 to $DF00 and jump into the expedition initializer at $8049.

Set the screen and VIC bank, prepare the IRQ and NMI, initialise the selected explorer and HUD, and show the title. On return from the title, seed the expedition time and the initial map position before entering the game loop.

Wait for the raster handler's flag in $82 and clear it. Update nearby objects, player controls, inventory, time and screen transitions. Run the scene's actor updates using the current scene and three rotating sprite output offsets, then hand a pending horizontal step to the IRQ.
Two-byte map offset below the left edge of the visible playfield, updated by the horizontal scroll code.
Clear the byte range beginning at $035E through $03E7 before the expedition is set up.
Use twelve times the selector ID at $0300 to choose twelve parameter bytes, then copy them to $82FE-$8309.
Sprite colour chosen at startup by the explorer index in $0300.
Four sixteen-byte frames copied into $5460 by the alternate scenery updater.
Four eight-byte source frames for glyph $B5. The phase bits at $036A select the frame.
Clear the restore request at $0388. Restore the saved scene, player pose and range limits from $0389-$0391, then rebuild the scene and return to the frame wait.
Convert A to one or two decimal digits using subtraction by ten. Values 100 and above become zero. Print via the screen cursor at $73-$74, with a trailing blank after a one-digit number.
Subtract $20 from the input character byte, store the glyph at the screen cursor $73-$74, and advance the cursor. Preserve Y by writing it into the restoring LDY operand.
Put the requested sound ID in $80 and clear the active music flag at $08 so the IRQ consumes the request.
Save A in an immediate operand. Queue it through $80 if the song flag at $08 and the effects mode flag at $A2E7 are both clear.

When $03E5 is zero, alternate on $03E6 and decrement minutes at $0365. Borrow through hours and days using 59 and 23 as wrap values. At expiry clear the clock and switch the scene and movement state to the timeout sequence.

Preserve A, X and banking. Check CIA2 timer A's interrupt bit and alternate the branch at $8758 between offsets zero and three. The zero-offset path waits for the raster high bit, then rearms the timer. The other path performs VIC updates at $877B.
Enable all eight sprites, clear extended-colour mode and bit 7 in the control write, and select 40-column single-colour mode before restoring the interrupted state.

Preserve A, X, Y and banking. Acknowledge the raster source, cycle the phase counter modulo six and patch the branch at $87BE to select one of six jumps. The non-raster path reads CIA1 interrupt status.
Branch displacement written by $87BB from three times the current IRQ phase. The six targets begin at $87C0 and are three bytes apart.

Set playfield colours, fine X scroll and visible screen base. Update sprite pointers and coordinates, schedule the following phase and set the loop flag. The sound dispatch at the end depends on the music and request state.
Set the next raster compare from A and return by restoring Y, banking, X and A.

Consult scene-specific scroll limits and the requested step at $9E. Change the fine scroll accumulator and swap the two sets of screen pointers at a character boundary. The phase may also prepare a hidden column or select the appropriate colour shift.
Schedule raster $B5. If the scroll phase flag and sprite initialisation flag allow it, call the explorer sprite frame generator at $A2FB.
Delay to the split and select $D018=$0E, a fixed fine scroll and the HUD palette. Schedule the next phase at raster $B9.
Install the hardware IRQ and NMI vectors in RAM and set up the VIC raster IRQ. Initialise the interrupt phase and leave the processor port with I/O banked away.
Shift each playfield colour row left in place. Patch high bytes of character reads for the active screen and take new rightmost cell colours from the $1800 table.
Operand of the character read feeding the first six rows of new rightmost colours. The left shift writes the active screen page here before the colour loop.
Active screen page plus one, patched into the character read used for the middle six rows of the leftward colour shift.
Active screen page plus two, patched into the character read used by the last four rows of the leftward colour shift.
Sixteen bytes in VIC register order for the eight X/Y position pairs. The playfield IRQ copies them to $D000-$D00F.
Shift each playfield colour row right in place. Patch high bytes of character reads for the active screen and use the $1800 table to fill the leftmost colour.
Active screen high byte patched into the new leftmost-character lookup for the upper six rows.
Active screen high byte patched into the new leftmost-character lookup for the middle six rows.
Active screen high byte plus one patched into the new leftmost-character lookup for the last four playfield rows.

Draw the three displayed inventory slots and the held slot by choosing VIC pointers and colours. An empty slot $FF uses the fallback pointer and colour entry. Place the four sprites at a fixed HUD height and schedule line $D4.
Patched LDX operand that restores the inventory slot counter after the colour lookup uses X. The loop wraps when the index reaches 27.

Set the sprite pointers and colours for the HUD's inventory markers and explorer portraits. Use $0327 to choose how many remaining portrait slots are filled. Restore the frame's initial IRQ phase by scheduling line $FF.

Read active-low joystick port 1 before port 2 and translate its five bits via $9679. When neither is active use the keyboard scanner for the directional and fire actions. Return the logical bits in A and store them in $C4.
Thirty-two input-combination entries turn raw joystick directions and fire into the engine's direction and fire bits, cancelling opposing directions on either axis.
Thirteen port B strobes for the keyboard scan by logical key index.
Thirteen sense masks for the port A reads following the port B scan strobe.
Thirteen port A strobes for scanning the matrix in the reverse direction.
Thirteen sense masks for reverse-direction scans.
Use A as a key index and return the masked keyboard matrix result. Wait for two stable reads and use both scan directions for a zero result. Callers treat zero as pressed.

Reset the scene object slots and calculate the viewport. With $CF clear expand twelve map strips plus two wrap strips, substituting the explorer-specific strip for strip $28 in the first loop. With $CF set use the separate screen build. Both paths seed fine scroll from player X.

Expand strip A from its 32 tile IDs at $3500 + 32*A. Each tile contributes four by four character cells from $0800 + 16*ID. Store into the strip buffer at $86-$87 using a 448-character row stride, with subgroup rows separated by $01C0.
First strip number for each scene index. Six groups of twelve entries point at strips $00, $0C, $18, $24, $30 and $3C.
Transfer the first six, next six and final four visible rows from the expanded map to both screen buffers. Look up the colour byte per glyph at $1800 and store it into VIC colour RAM.

Use the scene index and player X for the starting scroll address. Adjust subcell X to 3 or 4, normalize a negative coarse offset, and use the scene's override viewport word when the player is outside the standard scroll bounds.
Swap the live colour lookups at $1880-$18FF with the alternate group at $3E00-$3E7F.

Select one of two character update paths using the scene mode at $03E8. The ordinary path copies eight bytes into glyph $B5 at $4DA8. The alternate path updates two glyphs at $5460 and two bytes at $57EA.
Save the current scene, action, player position, pose and scene limits to $0389-$0391. The restore branch at $85D0 reads these fields before rebuilding the scene.
Indexed by scene number at $9D97. A nonnegative flag permits a checkpoint save when the additional state at $036D is clear.
Fill $0200-$02FF with bit-pair reversals, so the four multicolour pixels of a sprite byte can be read in reverse order by a table lookup. Also seed the two HUD labels through $9F79.
VIC sprite pointer values read by the playfield raster handler for the alternate frame case.
Zero $AF through $FF at expedition startup.
Copy two eight-character rows from $9F8B and $9F93 into the HUD screen.

Blank the title field, switch the VIC charset, draw its border and print the credits and controls. Keyboard key indices $0B and $0C change the music/effects mode. Fire clears the field, restores the display settings and releases the expedition startup code.
Store A from cell Y down to zero through screen pointer $73-$74.
Point the title printer at the control strings at $A168 and screen address $40FA, then fall through to the line printer.
Read characters through $71-$72 until zero. A carriage return advances to the next screen line, otherwise emit a glyph using $8666.
Printable control legend in PETSCII with carriage returns and a zero terminator. $A1D9 is the title's ten-byte music or effects status field.
Printable credit lines for Teque, Argus Press and the two programmers. Carriage returns separate display rows and zero ends the text.
Printable title message asking for side 2. $A085 selects it if $A2E8 is nonzero. The two-file RCS/HCC disk boot reached the credits path.
Ten-byte replacement label copied to the title when the title loop changes the audio mode.
Ten-byte replacement label copied to the same screen text when switching back to effects.
Title audio mode byte toggled by two keys. A set value suppresses the music request at the end of the title.
Title message selector read at $A085. Zero chooses credits and nonzero chooses the prompt at $A273.
Update the spare explorer sprite slot from the current animation frame, then exchange the active and spare sprite selector bytes.

Draw frame A using 63 bytes starting at $F036 + 63*A. Read three 21-byte columns and interleave them in the $5800 sprite slot. For a mirrored pose, reverse the three column positions and reverse the four pixels in each byte using the table at $0200.
Clear a sprite at $7500, then generate selected explorer frames $34-$3F and the explicitly chosen HUD and playfield frames $00-$02 and $1F before clearing the initialisation flag.

Generate selected frame A in the sprite buffer selected by $A2EA. Choose the destination pointer from the frame table for A at least $20 or use caller X below $20, then copy the 64-byte slot into the VIC bank.
Clear the music-active flag and the three SID control bytes. Discard the return address of the event decoder's immediate caller so the normal voice output path is skipped.
Transfer each ready voice's buffered frequency, pulse width, waveform and envelope bytes to its SID register group. Apply the stored filter and volume fields.
Switch out I/O before the shared sequence decoder runs, then restore the expected banking through the output path.
Save A as the sequence selector, reset SID voice control and decoder state, seed the sound work areas and mark the player active.
Count down waits per voice and load the selected sequence pointers for two or three voices. Decode their next events and enter the SID output stage.

Decode the active pattern or start a new pattern from the sequence. Track repetitions, command parameters and note state in the voice's zero-page slots. A sequence terminator branches to channel shutdown.

Advance the current voice's pattern index and use the note and instrument state to update its buffered pitch and modulation. Layer the voice's current effect parameters over the note before the SID write stage.
Patched zero-page operand of the indexed pattern read at $A7B5. The decoder sets it to the current voice's pointer before reading the note or command.
Use the current voice's pattern index and its sequence pointer in zero page to return the next parameter byte.
Track selector table containing little-endian sequence pointers in six-byte rows. The sound tick reads one pointer per participating voice.
Byte streams reached through the title and effects sequence pointers. The decoder selects patterns with low bytes, interprets high bytes as sequence commands and stops on $FF.
Low bytes of the pattern pointers selected by sequence pattern number at $A695.
High bytes paired with $AD5A and read by $A69A.
Note and control streams entered through the pattern pointer tables. $A623 reads a pattern through the current voice's zero-page pointer until its $FF terminator.
Update the two-byte pseudo-random state at $B18A-$B18B using the previous state and a lookup from sprite data. Return a derived byte in A and restore Y.

Update the sprites belonging to scene $28. Select their output slots through $81DF and use $CC for the group state flag. Initialise the pictures and coordinates on first use and maintain them on later updates. The routine can request the scene sound.
When the current player is idle at exactly ($C0,$40) and presses right, reach the following scene-specific handler.
When $0368 permits it, initialise or update the scene's sprite at slot $837E plus the current group offset.
Clear the action inhibit flag, then test the active scene, the player's X band and Y, and the held item for the scene's special response.
Initialise the scene's actor sprite near ($A0,$48). Use the current scene and actor phase to update its picture, coordinates and player interaction.
Special actor frame sequence indexed by the player action tick divided by four. Zero advances the scene actor's state.
Initialise the scene's sprite at ($C8,$48). On approaching the actor, compare the held item with $83 to choose the branch that hides the actor or starts a player response.
Initialise and advance paired sprite slots using the current group state. This handler returns when $0368 is set.
Initialise the scene sprite on opposite sides depending on the sign of $039E, then update the sprite and response state.
Move a sprite one unit left until X falls below $09. Update its Y in the early and late X bands and indicate a step in $71.
Initialise the actor at ($A4,$40) and update the actor and held-item interaction using the counters and IDs in the scene's work area.
Enter the paired-sprite update with the rate parameter $02.
Copy three startup sprite records on its first pass, then update the associated sprites from the scene's state.
In the active scene, test object proximity and the held item against $039A. A match clears the held item, adds 150 points and increments the successful delivery counter. On its sixth hit enter $B9BE.
Set scene $28, set the alternate scene and clock suppression flags, choose movement and pose bytes and enter the scene rebuild path at $8715.
At Y=$20 and X from $76 through $83, check for held item $8D before the scene's player-action test.
Set X to $08 for the scene's actor before the shared sprite and interaction code.
Set X to $DC before the shared actor logic, which sets Y to $12 and selects a frame using $03A3.
Count to $14 in the active scene. Once there, $039D controls whether the counter advances and requests action $17.
At Y cell band $38, use bit zero of the $036A tick counter to gate the update. Convert player X to a character column and update the scene's associated cells.
Select a code address from the scene dispatch table at $BB1B and patch the jump at $BB18. Scene $28 may use an explorer-specific substitution. Pass the sprite output grouping in $CC.
Little-endian code targets for the jump at $BB18. Index twice the effective scene number in the handler selector.
Compare the current and effective scene IDs and return normally when they match. On mismatch, strip the caller's return address before RTS.
Apply the scene $30 special-case item use, then update inventory navigation and check the swap key. On a fresh swap press, exchange the held item at $0328 with the highlighted slot selected by $0381.
Dispatch scene-specific inventory interactions in scenes $19, $3A and $10.
Handle the item and scene checks shared by scenes $19 and $3A, including the held $8F case and scene-specific progress state.
Test the two candidate pickup records for the current scene. The runtime records begin at $D262.

Test proximity to the candidate record, skip empty IDs and find a free slot in the 27-slot inventory. Apply item-dependent flags, modify the pickup's state and add the corresponding score where applicable.
Match held item $8C and the scene's Y and X bands, then advance the local object state and update the affected cells.
Thirty-six mutable 14-byte actor records for the current map group, three per scene. $C2E7 expands the packed source data here and $C3A2 dispatches and writes back the active scene's three records.
Clear 504 bytes at $C0EF. Expand 36 four-byte records from $C6E5 + 12*A into 14-byte actor records, separating the packed type, orientation and other flag fields.

Locate the scene's three actor records in the expanded group. Copy position and direction for each used type. Keep an existing output frame $55, substitute $7F for an output frame $FF, and otherwise copy the record's frame. Call the actor handler and write the four resulting fields back.
Actor handler jump whose low and high target bytes are rewritten by $C3F1 and $C3F7.
Little-endian update routine addresses indexed by twice the actor type. Type $0F is skipped before the dispatch.
Mark the sprite output entry $8374,X as $7F and return.
Initialise the actor if needed and move its X coordinate two units in the current direction. Reverse the direction flag when the positional or terrain limit is hit.
Initialise the actor if needed and move its Y coordinate two units in the current direction. Reverse direction on the boundary or a terrain test.
Seed the actor's delay from the pseudo-random byte with the side flag preserved, then count its low seven bits down.
Hide the sprite while its spawn timer is pending. On expiry move it vertically by two units, consulting terrain and resetting the timer when it exits the playfield or reaches its stop case.
Ensure the sprite is initialised. Use the common sprite update path unless the frame is $55 or the hidden marker $7F.
Age the delay counter, then step through a back-and-forth frame sequence derived from bits of the actor phase. Reset the delay after sixteen animation steps.
Set the actor's initialization bit and copy its starting position, first picture and direction from the expanded actor record to the sprite work area.

Seventy-two scenes have three four-byte actor definitions each. The first byte packs the type in bits 0-3, a three-bit field in bits 4-6 and one flag in bit 7. The last byte is also split into an index and a direction bit during expansion.
Enter the scene-specific movement path, use the alternate pose, sample controls and adjust its local scroll counters and position.

Decode direction and fire and pass them through current pose, terrain and object rules. Adjust player coordinates, scroll request and orientation. Fire can start an airborne state when the action and terrain tests pass. Right and left may change the scene at their map boundaries.
Five explorer-dependent strip numbers used when the standard strip number is $28.
Find the current row in the region grid and rebuild the scene one row above with Y set near the lower edge. If it is already at the top, restore the coordinate backup.
Find the current row in the region grid and rebuild the scene one row below with Y set near the upper edge. At the bottom, restore the coordinate backup.
If the player action byte at $036E is nonzero, use it minus one to select a word at $D2C3. Patch the absolute jump target and enter the state handler if the word is nonzero.
Advance the scene index with wrap in its twelve-scene group and rotate the actor group state to match. The tail invokes the checkpoint condition.
At player X=$FF, reduce the scene index with wrap in its twelve-scene group and rotate the actor state to match. The tail invokes the checkpoint condition.
Clear bit 7 of the second byte in each packed pickup record at $D142 and $D1D2.
Set the active group's base scene and expand 24 two-byte placement records to four-byte work slots starting at $D262.

Separate the object's sprite ID and its packed coordinates. An empty record or a set removal flag produces $7F as the work-slot ID. For the specified explorer-dependent scene choose the replacement packed entry first.
First group of 72 scene pickup records. Each pair packs the object's identifier with X, Y and a removal flag, decoded by $D063.
Second group of 72 packed pickup records, at two bytes per scene as in the first group.
Twenty-four four-byte slots for the active group. The pickup checks use the unpacked X, Y and item ID in the first three bytes.
Thirty-three little-endian action handler addresses. $CEF5 indexes this table with twice the one-based action index minus two.
Advance the action counter and pose $3F. On the counter's $40 bit advance the relevant actor group state and clear the player action.
Advance the action counter and choose a frame using a triangular index formed from its low three bits.
Quarter-speed pose stream read by $D3DE until the $FF terminator.
Set the pose, preserve X, switch the map setup flag and rebuild the scene on the first action tick. Later ticks follow the action's remaining sequence.
Read an animation byte from $D34A at quarter speed. Output the pose until $FF, then advance the action and reset its tick counter.
Read the sequence at $D412 on the action tick counter. The $FF byte advances the action.
Quarter-speed pose stream read by $D3F8 until the $FF terminator.
Read the sequence at $D45A and request effect 4 on frame $31. The $FF byte completes this part of the action.
Quarter-speed pose stream for $D428. The caller tests for frame $31 before it checks the terminator.
Select pose and effect pairs at $D4CC and request six spare explorers before entering the shared sequence driver.
Set the next actor thresholds, select the sequence at $D4F3 and set the shared sequence's terminal spare-explorer count to four.
Select the sequence at $D4ED, queue effect 3 and enter the shared sequence.
Choose pose and effect pairs at $D4CE before entering the common sequence driver.
Read the pose selected by $71-$72 at one entry per four action ticks. On the terminator, optionally queue the effect supplied separately in $6F and switch to action $12.
Read a quarter-speed animation sequence at $D657. At the terminator realign Y to a character boundary and return to normal movement.
Quarter-speed poses for action $11. The handler aligns the player's Y at the $FF terminator.
After a five-tick wait, map held items $89, $9C and $9B to actions $0E, $0F and $10 and request a sound. A right input cancels the action.
Add one to X every update and subtract the indexed Y step from the motion table at $D75A. Request right scroll and advance the pose during the movement.
Reuse the upward movement path with a shorter duration and a second displacement table at $D802.
Advance right and move up on alternating four-tick groups. At the end, enter the next scene at ($08,$08) and request action $12.
168 unsigned vertical steps indexed by the action's tick count and subtracted from player Y.
64 vertical step values used by the shorter action sharing the same movement loop.
Display quarter-speed frames from $D8E6, then derive position offsets and the displayed hint value from the scene table at $CF1C. Queue the next action with the selected index.
Increment the player action tick counter and index the pose pointer by the old counter divided by four.
Read the pose at $71-$72 using a separate tick counter at $B9BD. Divide the old tick by four before indexing.
Probe terrain, preserve the scene index in the adjacent sprite state and branch according to whether the terrain result below the player is zero.
Set the action pose and call the collision scan. Handle movement and terrain contact using the current controls and action ID.
Subtract four from player Y. Cross to the region above if it becomes negative. Otherwise probe terrain and switch to action $02 when the floor class is zero.
Require held item $8A to continue the special movement path. With it, use directional input and collision tests to update the player's coordinates and scroll request.

Read the pose table at $DC14, advance the leap timer and use the displacement table at $DC38 for Y motion. Use the saved direction from $0370 for lateral movement with collision and scene wrap. Finish after the timer reaches $22 or on the landing path.
Use the action and phase index to subtract the signed delta at $DC38 from Y. Rebuild the neighbouring region if the new Y leaves the visible vertical band.
Read the pose pointer at $71-$72 indexed directly by the current action tick and write the explorer frame index.
Write A to the player action byte and reset its per-action counter to zero.
Per-tick pose numbers read by $DC00 from the leap handler.
Signed Y step bytes subtracted during the leap. $DBE5 checks vertical region boundaries after applying a step.
Store the supplied $73-$74 pointer in the mutable pose stream pointer at $DCD2.
Read a pose from the current stream and advance its pointer. When the byte is $FF clear the stream pointer instead.
Place the scene sprite at X=$24 and the associated Y. Check the player's relative Y, X band and action, then use control bits $04 and $08 to select action $13 or $14.
Scan logical key zero and request player action $0A on a pressed result.
Compare the current scene and player coordinates to three triples at $DE8D. Request action $16 on reaching the matching eight-unit X band at the specified Y.
Print hours, minutes and days at their HUD destinations using the decimal character emitter.
Compute the map coordinates used by the player collision probes from the scene number and the explorer's X and Y. Pass the probes a pointer to the four result bytes.

Locate the current terrain glyph and index its class through one of two 256-byte tables, selected by $03E8. A zero class continues to the next row. A negative class can enter the terrain response path.
Class byte for each character code when $03E8 is clear.
Second set of 256 collision class bytes, selected when $03E8 is nonzero.
Derive the row index from vertical offset $A8 and the column from horizontal offset $A9-$AA. Add the row base from $E41B.
Start with a clear result and probe the next three or four terrain cells vertically depending on the subcell Y. Consult collision classifications through the common probe.
Offset the player probe X by 23, point the output at the second result byte and call the common vertical terrain scan. Restore the output pointer afterward.
Start addresses of sixteen expanded map rows used by the collision cell lookup at $E2D2 and $E2D9.
Add the little-endian increment at $71-$72 to the score at $0376-$0377, then redraw the four-character score field.
Add the two-byte increment with carry from low to high to the score at $0376-$0377.
Compare the current and high scores as unsigned little-endian words. Store the current value and draw the high-score field if it is greater.
Subtract a decimal place value from the print accumulator while it is large enough and count the accepted subtractions in $6F.
Little-endian divisors 1000, 100, 10 and 1 for drawing the four score digits by repeated subtraction.
First sixteen 63-byte sprite frames from the chosen explorer. The frame generator reads the three 21-byte columns separately.
Frames $10-$1F for the selected explorer, at a 63-byte stride from $F036.
Frames $20-$2F for the selected explorer. The right-facing and reflected drawing paths can use the same source bytes.
Final sixteen frames $30-$3F from the transferred 4032-byte sprite block, ending at $FFF5.
